title: Digital Literacy and Reading Habits of the Central University of Tamil Nadu Students: A Survey Study
extended_summary:
This paper examines university students’ digital literacy skills and reading habits, with particular attention to whether students prefer print or digital reading materials and how they use various digital tools. The authors ask what students know and can do with digital technologies, how often they use specific digital environments and applications, and what formats they prefer for reading in different situations.

The study uses a quantitative survey design with a structured questionnaire administered to 135 students and research scholars at the Central University of Tamil Nadu in India. Participants included undergraduate, postgraduate, integrated UG/PG students, and research scholars. The survey collected self-reported data on typing, web searching, computer and internet literacy, use of digital environments (email, web, text chat, video conferencing, language apps), digital application skills, and reading preferences for print versus electronic formats.

Findings suggest that respondents generally rated themselves as good or very good in several digital literacy dimensions and frequently used common digital tools, especially email, text chatting, and the web. At the same time, print remained the preferred format for many reading purposes, such as reading in bed, reading for pleasure, and reading with children, while electronic formats were preferred for travel, sharing, and quick access to new material. The authors conclude that students are comfortable with digital media and value digital literacy, but still rely on print for many reading activities.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic category of generative AI / LLM chatbot tools used for producing and interacting with text, language, and information in conversational form.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper does not study a generative AI tool. It is a survey of students' digital literacy, digital device use, and reading habits, with one item mentioning mobile apps for language learning but no named AI system.

quality_tier_rationale: The paper is a cross-sectional survey about digital literacy and reading habits, not an evaluation of an AI tool. It reports descriptive frequencies and self-ratings, with no experimental or quasi-experimental design.
impact_tier_rationale: No AI intervention or outcome effect is measured, so there is no evidence of impact attributable to a tool.
